owner: Not yet named; the compliance committee reviews it and the board approves it
next_review: Date for the board to set; the scribe rollout decision comes after the pilot, in about three months.
why: We want AI to take paperwork off staff, like charting at night. We must protect patient information and keep people making every decision.
who_it_covers: Staff, clinicians, volunteers, contractors and board members at both clinics.

tools.name: AI scribe from our health record vendor
tools.approved_for: Visit notes for the three pilot providers; signed business associate agreement, so it may hold patient information.

tools.name: OpenEvidence and UpToDate AI search
tools.approved_for: Clinical questions only; no patient information.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.approved_for: General letters and handouts; no patient, donor or staff information, even names.

new_tools: Approvers are listed below. Anything that could touch patient information needs a signed business associate agreement first, no exceptions.
allowed_uses: Look up a clinical question, like first-line treatment, with no patient information
Draft patient handouts for clinician review, and reminder or sliding fee letters with no names
Pilot providers: let the scribe draft visit notes, after the patient agrees

needs_approval.use: Any new tool or AI feature that could touch patient information
Any other new tool, add-on or AI feature

protected_information: Diagnoses, medications, behavioral health notes, substance use treatment records, HIV status, reproductive health, immigration status, sliding fee income documents, insurance numbers, staff files, and the donor list (some donors are patients).
off_limits: Never put patient information into ChatGPT, Google Translate or any tool not approved for it above.
Don't use AI in secret. If you're unsure, ask your manager.
check_before_it_goes_out: Providers read every word of a scribe note before signing. AI has added medications we decided against.
A clinician reviews AI-drafted handouts for facts, names and numbers. Whoever sends AI-assisted work is responsible for it.
decisions_about_people: A clinician decides and signs all care, and a person decides sliding fee eligibility. AI may only look things up or draft for review.
being_open: Tell patients when the scribe is listening and let them say no, using the verbal consent script.
If we add a chatbot, patients must be told it is not a person.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell Nadia right away if patient information may have gone into an AI tool. She runs the HIPAA breach clock.
Reporting a mistake is expected, not punished.
who_owns_this: The compliance committee reviews this policy, then the board approves it. Your manager explains it; ask if unsure.
open_questions: After the pilot, do we roll the scribe out to all providers, and should behavioral health use it at all?
Do we formally approve ChatGPT, OpenEvidence and UpToDate AI search? Beth called the scribe our only approved AI.
Who checks AI-assisted Spanish materials, may we use Google Translate, and may AI suggest billing codes? Who approves?
How will we answer funders about AI, reassure staff about phone bots, and set the policy owner and review schedule?
